text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein says on return to Jordan after surgery in the United States on an enlarged prostate "my health is good and the results have been positive"; extends his thanks to Jordanians for their feelings.
- Preparations for parliamentary elections begins next week; Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali to meet deputies to exchange views.
- Islamic Action Front (IAF) head Ishaq al-Farhan dismisses possibility of a joint platform with leftists and nationalists in the run up to national elections next November.
- Tribe of the soldier who shot Israeli school girls send a cable of support to the Hashemite ruling family; they express full confidence in the military court which Daqamsa will stand trial in soon.
- Islamists begin preparations for the coming elections; their leadership orders grassroots begin to sort out potential candidates.
- Majali to hold his first press conference since becoming Prime Minister on Saturday; premier to tackle the king's visit to U.S., internal issues and Jordan's Arab ties.
- Jordanian investors plan a new multi-million dollar pharmaceutical company.
- Jordan to get $2.5 million of export credit from the United States.
- Al Aswaq organises the Jordanian Women's Football Tournament, the first of its kind in the kingdom which will be held under the patronage of Prince Abdullah and Princess Rania.
- Hashemite charity donates 50,000 dinars ($70,621) to Jerusalem fund raising campaign launched by MBC television network.
- Crown prince says economic and social security more important than military might.
